clue.text: Last Plantagenet free to catch fish

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so one word closes round the other

blocks.note: to rid is to free or clear
the char is a trout-like fish

explanation.surface: A freed angler about to land a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Plantagenet dynasty ended when Richard III fell at Bosworth in 1485.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard III, killed in battle in 1485, was the final English monarch from that royal house.

clue.text: Floating structure right behind

blocks.note: R abbreviates right
aft means behind, towards the stern

explanation.surface: A floating platform lies just behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat platform of logs or planks that floats on water.

clue.text: Possibility large choir will sing here

blocks.note: a chance is a possibility
L abbreviates large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: There is a good chance a big choir will perform here.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, where the choir stalls stand.

clue.text: Special terms mythical craft dictated

indicators.note: something dictated is spoken out for writing down, so we go by sound

blocks.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth; the final T of the answer is silent

explanation.surface: Technical language about a legendary vessel being read out.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or slang of a particular group, its own special vocabulary.

clue.text: Find fault with stray dog in sea

indicators.note: stray means wandering off course, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a stray dog swimming in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Find fault looks like criticise, but it means find what is wrong, as a doctor or mechanic does.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to identify the cause of a problem, a technical sense of locating a fault.

clue.text: Arab king on time meeting American exhibitionist

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the king comes after the rest

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
US for American
Ibn Saud founded the Saudi Arabian monarchy

explanation.surface: A Saudi monarch keeps an appointment with an American who loves to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame Tussaud founded the London waxworks; she was an exhibitor, so the definition plays on 'exhibitionist' as a show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Tussaud ran a famous wax figure display, making her literally a person who stages exhibitions.

clue.text: Herbal infusion Bond found outside health farm

indicators.note: one word sits on the outside of the other, wrapping round it

blocks.note: a tie is a bond
san is short for sanatorium

explanation.surface: James Bond is spotted outside a spa with a cup of herbal tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond suggests 007, but here it simply means a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a tea made by steeping herbs or flowers in hot water.

clue.text: Form of sonata in Janacek’s first work for theatre

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the composer's name
a new form of the words means their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the initial of the Czech composer

explanation.surface: A sonata form in a Janáček composition written for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Joan is George Bernard Shaw's 1923 play about Joan of Arc, a stage drama.

clue.text: Silly one dragged inside when one over the eight

indicators.note: pulled into the middle of the words that follow

blocks.note: as means when
I is the Roman numeral one
one more than eight

explanation.surface: A daft drunk being hauled indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: One over the eight is British slang for slightly drunk, but here it is read literally as eight plus one.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means extremely stupid, like the proverbial donkey or ass.

clue.text: Bloomer made by attorney — veil was lifted?

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney in the US
a mask veils the face
rose is the past tense of rise

explanation.surface: A lawyer's blunder exposed when a cover was raised.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer reads as a blunder but means something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The damask rose is a fragrant old garden rose, a flowering plant prized for its scent.

clue.text: Female called Lisa deciphered hybrid language

indicators.note: deciphering a coded name means rearranging its letters into sense

blocks.note: F abbreviates female
rang as in telephoned
the name rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman phoned someone called Lisa and cracked a code.
explanation.definitionFit: Franglais mixes French with English borrowings, a blended tongue of two languages.

clue.text: Expression in papers the writer abroad recalled

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the French phrase runs backwards

blocks.note: identity papers
French for me, the writer, in a foreign tongue

explanation.surface: A foreign author remembers a phrase that appeared in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a set phrase whose meaning is not literal, a fixed turn of speech.

clue.text: Whip’s foolish action involves moving Mandelson finally

indicators.note: foolish suggests behaving senselessly, so the word beside it is jumbled
the last letter of Mandelson is shifted to a new position within the word for involves

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
to entail is to involve

explanation.surface: A political whip's daft move ends up dragging in Peter Mandelson.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTION is scrambled to CATONI; in ENTAILS the N (last letter of Mandelson) moves to the front, giving NETAILS. A party whip is the surface; the real whip is a lash. Mandelson is a Labour politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails is a knotted multi-thonged lash once used for flogging sailors and prisoners.

clue.text: Church in check with cross strengthened

indicators.note: in places the church abbreviation inside the word for cross

blocks.note: to rein is to check or restrain
to ford is to cross a river
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church inspection with a crucifix, its walls shored up.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforced describes something made stronger by added support or material.

clue.text: One praising Brussels agenda holds work back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for work in the other direction
the list holds something inside it, wrapping round it

blocks.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union
an agenda is a list of items
to go is to work or function

explanation.surface: European Union officials keep postponing a piece of business on their agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogist delivers speeches or writing in high praise, often of someone who has died.

clue.text: My word for doggie barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a dog that will not stop yapping.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like a dog's noise but is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or dismay, interchangeable interjections.

clue.text: Person affected problem storing uranium

indicators.note: storing means keeping something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a poser is a puzzling question
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Someone harmed by a difficulty over nuclear fuel storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person affected' reads like a victim, but affected here means pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur puts on airs, adopting a pretentious manner to impress others.

clue.text: Porridge served with fruit something sticky

blocks.note: porridge and bird are both British slang for time in prison
a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Oatmeal topped with fruit turns into a gluey mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge looks like breakfast, but in British slang it is a prison sentence, as is bird (from bird-time, rhyming slang).
explanation.definitionFit: Birdlime is a glue smeared on branches to trap small birds, an adhesive substance.

clue.text: Legendary ruler regularly sneers at poor

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: the even letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone routinely sneers at those who have less.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestor was the aged king of Pylos in Homer's epics, a mythical monarch famed for wise counsel.

clue.text: Metal point handling pressure in tower

indicators.note: handling means holding in the hands, so the outer word grips the pressure letter

blocks.note: an alloy of iron
E is a point of the compass
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A metal spike under strain on a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall pointed tower on a church.

clue.text: Book to secure hotel in sensational complaint

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: Titus is a book of the New Testament
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: Reserving a hotel room ends in a lurid grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: Sensational reads as lurid, but here it means to do with the senses: tinnitus is a hearing disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinnitus is a ringing in the ears, an ailment affecting the sense of hearing.

clue.text: Fuss about fleet initially adrift in storm

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word next to it
about means around, so the fuss surrounds the letters that follow

blocks.note: a to-do is a fuss
the Royal Navy, Britain's fleet
the first letter

explanation.surface: A panic over ships drifting loose in a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, a type of storm.

clue.text: Garden vegetable: it should be cut in haste

indicators.note: cut means removed, so the word it names comes out

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters are removed
celerity is speed or haste

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: harvest this vegetable quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a plant grown in kitchen gardens for its edible crisp stalks.

clue.text: Be in debt to no good bank — that restricts Old West hero

indicators.note: the bank restricts, or hems in, the short pair of letters that follows

blocks.note: to owe is to be in debt
N abbreviates no
G abbreviates good
a bank is a lender
O abbreviates old
W abbreviates west

explanation.surface: A cowboy hero owes money to a bank that is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: Old West suggests a cowboy, but it only supplies two letters; the hero is Owen Glendower, the Welsh leader who rebelled against Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Owain Glyndŵr, anglicised Owen Glendower, was a medieval Welsh rebel leader, celebrated as a national champion.

clue.text: Drinking punch, people in general like milk

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: we as in all of us
a hit is a punch

explanation.surface: Most people prefer their punch with milk in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch looks like a drink beside drinking, but it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk is white, so white describes something with the colour of milk.

clue.text: Divine female and male live together

indicators.note: together means side by side, so the two pieces are joined

blocks.note: he is a male pronoun
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A goddess and a man cohabiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth, cupbearer to the gods.

clue.text: Last pair to leave fancy island resort

indicators.note: the final two letters depart, cutting the word short

blocks.note: a caprice is a whim or fancy

explanation.surface: A couple are the last guests to leave a smart holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples, a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Mrs Harker’s cream-covered take out?

indicators.note: something covered has another layer wrapped round it

blocks.note: Mina Harker is the heroine of Bram Stoker's Dracula
the cream is the best, the elite

explanation.surface: Mina Harker in a cream-covered takeaway dish, hinting at Dracula's appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: Take out is gangster slang for kill, which fits Dracula's victim.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out someone is to kill or remove them, which is exactly to eliminate.

clue.text: Cook bass and young salmon?

blocks.note: a bass voice or note is deep
fry are young fish, including salmon

explanation.surface: A recipe question: how to cook sea bass and salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: Bass looks like the fish, but it means low in pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To deep-fry is to cook food by immersing it fully in hot fat or oil.

clue.text: Monstrosity the writer witnessed in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: the writer is I, and witnessed is saw; in a non-rhotic accent the pair sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: An author reports seeing something hideous on television.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, such as an unsightly building.
